estimators.label: DIMPLE JSD (bw 30 µm), tumor ↔ immune
estimators.note: a separation distance, so the sign is inverted relative to G and ΔG

sensitivity.verdict: On the MHC-II axis DIMPLE's JSD and uncorrected G both separate the groups at p ≈ 3e-4, and the JSD effect survives adjustment for cell counts. This portal's permutation-corrected ΔG does not (p = 0.33). The label-permutation null conditions on the point pattern, so it absorbs the part of the infiltration difference that is carried by where immune cells sit relative to tissue architecture. ΔG is the more conservative statistic and on this contrast it is too conservative.

reference: Masotti M, Osher N, Eliason J, Rao A, Baladandayuthapani V. DIMPLE: an R package to quantify, visualize, and model spatial cellular interactions from multiplex imaging with distance matrices. Patterns 2023;4:100879. Application cohort: VectraPolarisData HumanLungCancerV3 (Johnson et al. 2021), the same 153 patients used here.

headline.note: The two implementations differ only in which edge correction they apply: the package uses spatstat's diggle = TRUE, dividing each point by the correction at that point, while the Python version divides the smoothed surface by a smoothed window indicator. The residual is a boundary effect, which is why it is small and one-signed rather than noisy.
